rotationLink.why: following from gen 1 skips record 1 and reaches gen 3

rotationLink.name: reverse
rotationLink.why: either direction: gen 3 is linked to gen 0, which its chain leads back to

rotationLink.name: reverse-one-step
rotationLink.why: either direction: gen 2 is linked to gen 1

rotationLink.name: other-user
rotationLink.why: the records belong to u-bob, and the question is about u-carol

rotationLink.name: broken-chain-after-the-target
rotationLink.why: toFP is reached at record 1, but record 2 breaks the chain, so no link

rotationLink.name: bad-signature-after-the-target
rotationLink.why: toFP is reached at record 2, but record 3 is badly signed, so no link

rotationLink.name: reverse-across-a-broken-chain
rotationLink.why: gen 2 to gen 0 with record 2 skipped past: record 3 does not follow, so no link

rotationLink.name: wrong-user-record-in-the-list
rotationLink.why: a record for u-carol among u-bob's records refuses the whole list

rotationLink.name: fork-in-the-list
rotationLink.why: two different records with seq 1 refuse the list, even though gen 1 is reached

followPin.name: new-no-rotations
followPin.why: no pin and no records: the pin starts at rotSeq 0

followPin.name: new-latest-record-matches
followPin.why: no pin, and the latest record's new keys are the current ones: the pin starts at that record

followPin.name: new-earlier-record-matches
followPin.why: no pin, and the current keys are the ones record 2 made: the pin starts at record 2

followPin.name: new-no-record-matches
followPin.why: no pin, and no record's new keys are the current ones: rotSeq 0

followPin.name: new-record-bad-newSig
followPin.why: no pin, and the matching record is not signed by its new keys: rotSeq 0

followPin.name: new-record-bad-sig
followPin.why: no pin, and the matching record is not signed by its old keys: rotSeq 0

followPin.name: new-record-of-another-user
followPin.why: no pin, and the matching record is u-carol's: it explains nothing for u-bob

followPin.name: new-record-seq-zero
followPin.why: no pin, and the matching record has seq 0, which the format never allows: rotSeq 0

followPin.name: matching-unverified
followPin.why: the pin is the current key: its state stands, and the records are not read

followPin.name: matching-verified
followPin.why: a verified pin on the current key stays verified, with its rotSeq and rotHead, and bad records are not read

followPin.name: rotated-one-step
followPin.why: an unverified pin and one rotation to the current key: rotated, recorded at that record

followPin.name: rotated-verified-drops
followPin.why: a verified pin followed through three rotations becomes unverified, at the last record

followPin.name: rotated-from-rotSeq
followPin.why: a pin accepted at record 1 follows records 2 and 3, and records the third

followPin.name: fork
followPin.why: the record at rotSeq hashes to another head: changed, and the fork is reported

followPin.name: fork-two-records-at-a-seq
followPin.why: the user signed two different records 2: changed, and the fork is reported

followPin.name: rollback
followPin.why: the records omit the one at rotSeq: changed, and the rollback is reported

followPin.name: rollback-no-records
followPin.why: rotSeq is 1 and no records are served: changed, and the rollback is reported; the next pin has rotSeq 0

followPin.name: broken-chain
followPin.why: record 2 is skipped past, so the chain breaks: no error, but the chain explains nothing and the key is changed

followPin.name: bad-signature-in-chain
followPin.why: record 2 is signed by other keys: changed with no error, and the next pin is at rotSeq 0 because its record does not verify

followPin.name: chain-ends-elsewhere
followPin.why: the chain ends at gen 2 and the current keys are gen 4, as after a password-only reset: changed

followPin.name: chain-older-than-the-pin
followPin.why: every record predates the pin, and the current key is none of them: changed
